title: 5.4 Infectious Diseases
description: Infectious diseases, pathogens, transmission, and prevention

questions.question: What is an infectious disease?
options: A disease caused by disease-causing organisms that can be transmitted from person to person
It contains very large, multinucleated cells that challenge the definition of a single cell
They contain their own DNA and reproduce independently within the cell, similar to bacteria
The indigestible part of plants that helps prevent constipation and keeps the colon healthy
questions.answer: A disease caused by disease-causing organisms that can be transmitted from person to person

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of pathogens that cause infectious diseases?
options: It has no effect on the nervous system
All cells come from pre-existing cells
They prevent other plants from growing
Bacteria, viruses, protozoa, and fungi
questions.answer: Bacteria, viruses, protozoa, and fungi

questions.question: Which of the following is a method of transmission for infectious diseases?
options: An organism that carries a disease-causing organism and transmits it from one person to another
Direct contact with a patient, contaminated water or food, insect bites, and sexual intercourse
Vesicles are small membrane-bound sacs for transport; vacuoles are larger storage compartments
A dense region inside the nucleus where rRNA is synthesized and ribosome subunits are assembled
questions.answer: Direct contact with a patient, contaminated water or food, insect bites, and sexual intercourse

questions.question: What is a vector in the context of infectious diseases?
options: Direct contact with a patient, contaminated water or food, insect bites, and sexual intercourse
Vesicles are small membrane-bound sacs for transport; vacuoles are larger storage compartments
A dense region inside the nucleus where rRNA is synthesized and ribosome subunits are assembled
An organism that carries a disease-causing organism and transmits it from one person to another
questions.answer: An organism that carries a disease-causing organism and transmits it from one person to another

questions.question: Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by which pathogen?
options: Secondary occurs only in aquatic ecosystems
Shrubs → grasses → mosses → lichens → trees
A naming system using only the species name
Bacterium called Mycobacterium tuberculosis
questions.answer: Bacterium called Mycobacterium tuberculosis

questions.question: How is tuberculosis (TB) primarily transmitted?
options: To evaluate the quality and validity of research before publication
Through airborne droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes
The DNA-protein complex that makes up chromosomes during interphase
To stain the nucleus and other organelles, making them more visible
questions.answer: Through airborne droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes

questions.question: What is the name of the vaccine used to prevent tuberculosis?
options: MMR vaccine
BCG vaccine
Hepatitis B vaccine
Polio vaccine
questions.answer: BCG vaccine

questions.question: Malaria is caused by which type of pathogen?
options: Fungus called Aspergillus
Protozoan called Plasmodium
Bacterium called Vibrio cholerae
Virus called SARS-CoV-2
questions.answer: Protozoan called Plasmodium

questions.question: Which mosquito species acts as a vector for malaria?
options: Male Anopheles mosquito
Female Aedes mosquito
Female Anopheles mosquito
Infertility in both sexes
questions.answer: Female Anopheles mosquito

questions.question: Which of the following is a method to control malaria?
options: Pregnant women, nursing mothers, children, athletes, and people living with HIV/AIDS
Bacterial cell walls are made of cellulose; plant cell walls are made of peptidoglycan
They are nutrient-dense and help address malnutrition in a culturally acceptable way
Reducing mosquito populations, avoiding mosquito bites, and using anti-malarial drugs
questions.answer: Reducing mosquito populations, avoiding mosquito bites, and using anti-malarial drugs

questions.question: What does HIV stand for?
options: It becomes a law immediately
Human Immunodeficiency Virus
Human Influenza Vaccine
Hereditary Immune Virus
questions.answer: Human Immunodeficiency Virus

questions.question: Which type of cells does HIV primarily infect and destroy?
options: A bacterial infectious disease
T-lymphocytes (helper T cells)
To control the light intensity
Autotrophic via photosynthesis
questions.answer: T-lymphocytes (helper T cells)

questions.question: How is HIV transmitted?
options: Through direct exchange of body fluids such as blood, semen, and breast milk
States whether the hypothesis is supported or rejected based on the evidence
It acts as a solvent and transport medium for substances throughout the body
Building teeth and bones, muscle contraction, and nerve impulse transmission
questions.answer: Through direct exchange of body fluids such as blood, semen, and breast milk

questions.question: Cholera is transmitted primarily through:
options: To provide a baseline for comparison
Reproductive organs present at birth
Because there are not enough species
Contaminated drinking water and food
questions.answer: Contaminated drinking water and food

questions.question: What disease is caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi?
options: Malaria
Tuberculosis
Biology alone
Typhoid fever
questions.answer: Typhoid fever

questions.question: COVID-19 is caused by which virus?
options: HIV
Ebola virus
SARS-CoV-2
Influenza virus
questions.answer: SARS-CoV-2

questions.question: How does COVID-19 primarily spread?
options: Through detection, screening, treatment, and palliative care, as well as healthy lifestyle choices
Through respiratory droplets released when an infected person breathes, talks, coughs, or sneezes
The insufficient, excessive, or imbalanced consumption of nutrients that leads to health problems
An organism that carries a disease-causing organism and transmits it from one person to another
questions.answer: Through respiratory droplets released when an infected person breathes, talks, coughs, or sneezes

questions.question: Which of the following is a common symptom of COVID-19?
options: Extreme temperature variation between day and night
All living things are composed of one or more cells
Fever, cough, tiredness, and loss of taste or smell
To support a wire gauze or apparatus during heating
questions.answer: Fever, cough, tiredness, and loss of taste or smell

questions.question: What is the difference between an epidemic and a pandemic?
options: Tobacco use, physical inactivity, harmful use of alcohol, and unhealthy diets
Prokaryotes are smaller (0.1-5 $\mu$m), eukaryotes are larger (10-100 $\mu$m)
The group that receives the treatment or has the independent variable applied
A pandemic is an epidemic that spreads across multiple countries or worldwide
questions.answer: A pandemic is an epidemic that spreads across multiple countries or worldwide

questions.question: Vaccination works by:
options: Making the body defend against disease-causing organisms
To mount the specimen for observation under a microscope
A two-part naming system consisting of genus and species
A lower temperature is needed for viable sperm formation
questions.answer: Making the body defend against disease-causing organisms

questions.question: Proper waste disposal helps prevent infectious diseases by:
options: Binomial nomenclature and hierarchical classification
Lactobacillus (a bacterium used in yogurt production)
Reducing the breeding sites for pathogens and vectors
It becomes turgid as water enters the cell by osmosis
questions.answer: Reducing the breeding sites for pathogens and vectors
